data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 integrates with SRC_003 by composing a temporal-ordering forbidden case (SRC_004: mutation moves the synchronous precondition check to an asynchronous post-provider-call position) with an identity-comparison forbidden case (SRC_003: mutation weakens the endpoint identity check to a partial match on school ID). The integration claims these are two faces of a single attack surface — the synchronous precondition check — because weakening identity comparison (SRC_003) is meaningful only if the check still executes before the provider call (SRC_004), and the temporal mutation (SRC_004) is detectable only if the identity comparison itself is correct (SRC_003). A unified suite skeleton that pairs both forbidden cases into one compound mutation — where the endpoint identity is homogenized AND the check is delayed to post-call — would expose whether the suite catches the compounded silent pass. This claim is REFUTED IF the temporal-ordering violation and the identity-homogenization violation are causally independent such that a suite catching one does not need the other, meaning no integration is required and separate, non-composed forbidden cases suffice.
